heroHeadline: ICE Officer Charged in Minneapolis Metro Surge Shooting as Senate Begins Markup on $71.7B ICE/CBP Bill; Record 73,000 in Detention; South Sudan Third-Country Deportation Notices Served
heroSubtitle: On May 18, 2026, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty charged ICE officer Christian Castro with four counts of second-degree assault for shooting through the front door of a Minneapolis home on January 14 during Operation Metro Surge, wounding Venezuelan man Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis — who was in the country lawfully — in a case of mistaken identity. The charges mark the first criminal accountability for the surge that deployed ~3,000 federal agents across Minneapolis and killed two U.S. citizens. Senate Judiciary and Homeland Security committees opened formal markup sessions May 18-19 on the $71.7B ICE/CBP reconciliation package, with Republicans racing to revise the $1B White House ballroom security provision and other sections struck by the Senate Parliamentarian as Byrd Rule violations (May 14-15) before a full floor vote and Trump's June 1 signing deadline. ICE detention remains at a record 73,000 — 84% above year-ago levels — with 30+ FY2026 deaths in custody and a three-to-two circuit court split on the constitutionality of mandatory detention heading toward Supreme Court review. DHS also served third-country deportation notices to detainees targeting South Sudan on May 19, the latest in a pattern of forced transfers to countries detainees have no ties to.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, and Congressional records
